I’m retrieving and following the exact hosted Skillplane “PR refetch fix” workflow for PR #570. I’ll pin the live PR/head state, preserve this checkout, and treat the refetched unresolved review threads—not cached timestamps—as authoritative.

The hosted Skillplane MCP capability is not available in this session, so the Skillplane contract requires the cached local workflow as the fallback. I’m loading that workflow now before touching PR or repository state.

PR #570 is open on `21nCo/nucleum`, targeting `dev`, at head `2c3d45ce…`. Its dedicated worktree already exists at `/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus-pr-570-review`; I’m verifying that checkout is clean and exactly matches the live PR head before taking the single review snapshot.

The snapshot is larger than one GitHub page: PR #570 has 145 review threads, so I’m paging the GraphQL connection as required. I’m reducing each thread to its current unresolved comment, path, line, commit, and URL so classification is complete without losing the actionable text.

The complete snapshot is now pinned: 145 threads total, 64 unresolved across both pages, 56 reviews, 8 issue comments, and 160 inline comments. Most older unresolved threads have later fix commits but were never marked resolved, so I’m now checking the 64-thread queue against the exact `2c3d45ce…` source—starting with current-line validity and the latest review summaries.

The latest-head classification has narrowed the genuinely current queue to recovery/account isolation and policy issues; the newest commit already closes several prior comments (E2EE offlinability, PointGoal/node conversion, DataFn file reads, app-menu rollback, and backup awaiting). Before editing, I’m applying the repository’s required orientation and product-context checks to the remaining workflow surfaces.

Five findings remain current after checking the source and later fix commits: Surreal-backed legacy export, scoped legacy Flux deletion, app-menu namespace isolation, native download acknowledgement, and removal of newly added source comments. The other recent CodeRabbit items (CAS, type ownership, and collection no-op handling) are already present in `64885893`; I’m validating the exact legacy Surreal client API before implementing the recovery path.
